page.text:
Imposing the equational law of associativity on a magma yields a
*semigroup*. Associativity, $(a * b) * c = a * (b * c)$, guarantees that
grouping by parentheses does not affect the evaluation of a product.

By the *Generalized Associativity Theorem*, any string of $n$ elements
$a_1 * a_2 * \cdots * a_n$ evaluates to the exact same element regardless
of how parenthesizations are introduced. (The number of distinct
bracketings of $n$ factors is given by the Catalan number
$C_{n-1} = \frac{1}{n}\binom{2n-2}{n-1}$, all of which collapse to a
single value in a semigroup.) This allows us to dispense with parentheses
entirely. Prominent semigroups include the positive integers under
addition $(\mathbb{Z}_{>0}, +)$, strings under concatenation over an
alphabet $\Sigma^+$, and binary relations under relational composition.
